title: Free feature flags for coding agents
summary: Give your coding agent a prompt to add type-safe feature flags, targeting, and stable percentage rollouts with GrowthBook’s open-source SDK. No account needed.
body_markdown:
#### Ask your coding agent to hide an unfinished checkout and it can do that with one line of code.


If everyone should see the old checkout until the next deploy, a simple on/off switch is enough, and there’s nothing new to install.


Then someone asks, “Could we try it with 20% of Safari users in the UK?”


Either way, you’ll test that the right shoppers get the new checkout. If your agent builds the rollout logic from scratch, **your team also has to test and maintain the code that keeps each shopper in the same group on their next visit** .


**With GrowthBook’s**[free, open-source feature flag SDK](https://docs.growthbook.io/guides-for-agents/local-feature-flags-typescript#quick-start) **,** your agent still writes the rules in your repo. The SDK applies them inside your app using targeting and rollout logic that teams already run in production. **No GrowthBook account, API key, or connection to a flag server is required.**

## What your agent would otherwise build by hand


The hard part of “20%” is what happens when a shopper refreshes halfway through paying. Pick a random number on every page load and they could start in one checkout and finish in another.


- **“Just Safari users in the UK.”** Your app supplies the browser and country. Your agent defines the audience once, and the cart and checkout can both use the same flag.
- **“Start with 20% of them.”** The SDK uses a stable ID to give each eligible shopper the same checkout on repeat visits. Widen the rollout to 50% and the original group stays in.
- **“Why is the old checkout still showing?”** A typo like` newChekout` is easy to overlook in review. With typed flags, TypeScript catches the misspelled name before the change ships.
- **“Everyone’s on the new checkout. Can we delete the flag?”** Remove the flag from the project’s types and TypeScript points to the code that still reads it. Your agent has a concrete list of places to clean up.


You can review the audience and rollout percentage in the same pull request as the checkout itself. Jeremy Dorn explains[how the SDK catches those typos](https://www.growthbook.io/blog/building-a-type-safe-sdk-with-the-register-pattern) if you’re curious about the TypeScript behind it.


## Try it with one flag


Pick a feature you’d like a few people to try. Give your agent the setup guide and it can add the flag, set the audience, and test who gets each version.


[Open the Agent Guide](https://docs.growthbook.io/guides-for-agents/local-feature-flags-typescript)


## Copy prompt for your coding agent


Open the project where you want your first flag, then give your agent this prompt. You can also[copy it directly from the guide](https://docs.growthbook.io/guides-for-agents/local-feature-flags-typescript#give-this-guide-to-your-coding-agent) .


Read the full prompt


```text
Add feature flags with targeting and percentage rollouts to this project
using a local flags.ts file and the GrowthBook SDK, following
https://docs.growthbook.io/guides-for-agents/local-feature-flags-typescript


Read the guide in full before editing. Create flags.ts with the AppFeatures
and AppAttributes types, a payload typed as Payload, and the
Register declaration. Load it with the GrowthBook SDK and read every flag
through the SDK. You do not need to create a GrowthBook account or add a
client key. Never put secrets or personal data in flags.ts.


Return: the flags you added, their default values and rules, the files you
changed, and how you verified that each flag evaluates as intended.
```

Have your agent show you the checkout in three situations:


- A UK Safari shopper in the rollout sees the new checkout
- Someone outside the UK sees the old checkout
- Both can refresh the page halfway through paying and stay in the checkout they started in

## When you need to turn a flag off between deploys


There’s one good question to ask before you keep a flag in Git. If checkout starts failing on Saturday, can the person on call wait for a deploy? With a local flag, changing the rules means shipping a code change.


If that wait is too long, move the flag definitions into GrowthBook Cloud or a self-hosted instance. Connect the SDK and the flag checks your agent already put in the app keep working, and your team can now manage the rollout as it happens.


- **Turn the new checkout off from a browser.** With[streaming updates](https://docs.growthbook.io/lib/js#streaming-updates) enabled, connected apps pick up the change without another deploy.
- **Find out which checkout works better.** Run an experiment and compare how many shoppers in each group finish paying.
- **Watch for payment failures.** On supported paid plans,[Safe Rollouts](https://docs.growthbook.io/features/safe-rollouts) can monitor a metric you choose and roll back the rule if it gets significantly worse.


If all you want today is to try the new checkout with a few shoppers, the local file is enough.[Give your agent the setup guide](https://docs.growthbook.io/guides-for-agents/local-feature-flags-typescript#give-this-guide-to-your-coding-agent) and pick the first group you want to try it with.


## Change flags between deploys


Give the person on call a way to turn off the new checkout from a dashboard. Connect your app to GrowthBook Cloud when you need that switch.
